title: Ecclesiastes Bible Quiz - Chapter 3
description: Ten questions on Ecclesiastes 3: a time for every purpose under heaven, eternity set in the heart, and man and animal returning to dust.

questions.text: How does the famous opening of this chapter run: "For everything there is a season, and a time for every..."?
questions.explanation: The first verse says: for everything there is a season, and a time for every purpose under heaven.

questions.text: According to this chapter, there is a time to be born and a time to what?
questions.explanation: The verse says there is a time to be born, and a time to die; a time to plant, and a time to pluck up that which is planted.

questions.text: There is a time to weep, and a time to what?
questions.explanation: The verse says there is a time to weep, and a time to laugh; a time to mourn, and a time to dance.

questions.text: There is a time to keep silence, and a time to what?
questions.explanation: The verse says there is a time to keep silence, and a time to speak.

questions.text: There is a time for war, and a time for what?
questions.explanation: The verse says there is a time to love, and a time to hate; a time for war, and a time for peace.

questions.text: What has God set in the hearts of men, according to this chapter?
questions.explanation: The verse says God has made everything beautiful in its time and has also set eternity in their hearts, yet so that man can't find out the work God has done.

questions.text: What does this chapter call it when a man eats, drinks and enjoys good in all his labor?
questions.explanation: The verse says that every man eating and drinking and enjoying good in all his labor is the gift of God.

answers.text: The burden of the sons of men

questions.text: What did the Preacher see in the place of justice under the sun?
questions.explanation: He saw that in the place of justice, wickedness was there, and in the place of righteousness, wickedness was there.

questions.text: According to this chapter, where do all go, since all are from the dust?
questions.explanation: The verse says all go to one place: all are from the dust, and all turn to dust again.

questions.text: What did the Preacher see that there is nothing better than, at the end of this chapter?
questions.explanation: He saw that there is nothing better than that a man should rejoice in his works, for that is his portion.

answers.text: That a man should rejoice in his works
That a man should seek great wisdom
That a man should leave his labor behind
That a man should see what comes after him
